situation (example wording): "Vermont murders per 100,000 in 2024 (NIBRS)", "Pennsylvania violent crime rate from NIBRS", a NIBRS state or national rate
what the app does today: A NIBRS state or national rate divides by the sum of the agencies' own NIBRS populations, a zero included (P62): 150 agencies hold a zero in 2024 where the Crime Index has a population (6.4 million people), so Vermont's and Pennsylvania's rates came out about 30% too high.
proposed behavior: A NIBRS state or national rate divides by the sum, over the agencies counted, of each agency's own NIBRS population where it is above zero, and the Crime Index population of that agency and year where NIBRS holds zero or no figure. Nothing changes for Current Trends or Historical, which use the Crime Index populations. An agency with neither has no population (the rate is withheld, as before). In 2024, 98.7% of the agencies in both files have identical populations; 61 differ by 0.4% in total.
exact default or choices offered: No question; the rate's note names the combined population as before.
why: Jeff 2026-11-21 (through the coordinator): the agency's own population from its NIBRS records, "though they should be identical" to the Crime Index; measured: identical for 98.7% of agencies, a zero in NIBRS for 150 agencies. Amends P62 and P90 (the current population of the Consistent Reporting Agencies follows the same rule).
test cases: The runner gate lists every NIBRS state or national rate that changes.
